elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Rendered §3.4: "Customer may terminate this Agreement (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment ... for convenience at the end of any calendar month". Service Option Attachments are the Order-Form-referenced attachments, so the Agreement-level and order-level convenience right both exist (subject only to the retained prerequisite-SOA carve-out).

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered clause (a): "providing at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice of such termination for convenience to IBM". The retained "at the end of any calendar month" effectiveness anchor is a timing restriction but does not lengthen the 30-day notice.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund language appears anywhere in the rendered text; the only money mechanic is Customer paying "the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments, capped at three (3) months' charges". To reach preferred, insert an express obligation on IBM to refund prepaid charges pro rata for the period after the effective date of termination.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: On the record supplied, IBM's only exits are non-renewal under §3.2 (notice at least 90 days before the end of the then-current term, operating within the auto-renewal sentence) and material breach under §3.3; no mid-term IBM convenience right appears in the cited or rendered language.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered clause (a) gives Customer a convenience right on "at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice", i.e. a notice burden lighter than the 60–90 day fallback ceiling; the underlying requirement (a Customer convenience right on notice no longer than 90 days) is satisfied. The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: false" is a mechanical miss caused by the parenthetical between "Service Option Attachment" and "for convenience"; in substance the right is expressly stated.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Rendered clause (b): "paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments, capped at three (3) months' charges." "Charges" is the fee term used throughout this IBM agreement, so the previously open-ended Attachment A charges are now bounded.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: §3.2 sits inside the auto-renewal sentence ("will renew automatically ... unless either party notifies ... at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term ... that it has elected to terminate"), so IBM's election operates as non-renewal effective at the end of the then-current term rather than a mid-term convenience exit; no other IBM convenience right appears.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: §3.2 requires the terminating party to notify "at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term", so any IBM term-end exit carries a 90-day notice.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: the cap in operation 2 fixes the only material fallback gap (open-ended Attachment A early termination charges), and the two Vendor-side elements are already satisfied by §3.2's term-end non-renewal mechanic plus the absence of any IBM mid-term convenience right.

Preferred is not complete: there is no pro-rata refund of prepaid charges. To press preferred, add to §3.4 an express IBM obligation to refund prepaid charges pro rata for the period after the effective date of termination.

Minimality fails on operation 1. The pre-existing "at least one month's prior written notice" already gave Customer a convenience right on notice well inside the 60–90 day fallback window, so no edit to the notice period was needed to reach the targeted level; rewriting it to "thirty (30) days' prior written notice of such termination for convenience" is a paraphrase of already-compliant, Customer-favourable language and also drafts below the fallback threshold the finding claims to target. Drop operation 1 and keep only the three-month cap (or, if the notice period is to be touched at all, do so under a preferred-level proposal that also adds the pro-rata refund).

Intent is preserved: the "end of any calendar month" effectiveness anchor, the prerequisite-SOA carve-out, the Attachment A / Service Option Attachment charge references, §3.2 renewal timing and §3.3 breach termination all survive without contradiction; the cap limits rather than orphans the charge mechanic.

Drafting note for repair: "three (3) months' charges" leaves the base slightly open (monthly charges for the terminated Service Option Attachment, aggregate charges, or averaged over which months). Tie it expressly to the average monthly charges payable under the terminated Service Option Attachment(s) over the three months preceding the notice to avoid a later dispute.
